title: Per-token Elasticity Experiment — Output-weighted Discounts & Synchronized Streaming Minimums
creator: Nina Patel
body:
Overview:
We want to run a controlled experiment to test a hybrid per-token pricing shape that: (1) applies modestly lower unit pricing for output tokens vs input tokens (output-weighted discounts), and (2) introduces a synchronized streaming minimum that only applies when streaming responses are active and a session-level microfloor is exceeded. The goal is to understand how directional token economics and streaming minimums impact ARPU, model selection, customer UX (latency vs. cost trade-offs), and revenue predictability for enterprise customers.

Hypotheses:
1) An output-weighted discount (e.g., 0.9x output price vs input baseline) will encourage customers to shift compute toward model outputs (e.g., longer responses), improving perceived value and increasing average revenue per session by at least 6% among engaged cohorts.
2) A synchronized streaming minimum (microfloor applied only when streaming is active and per-session output tokens exceed X) will reduce billing surprises and lower churn from small-burst streaming while preserving revenue for sustained streams.
3) The combined change will increase total hosted API revenue by >3% in treatment cohorts without materially increasing cost/unit (expected cost delta <2%), due to higher output token share and predictable minimums.

Experiment design:
- Cohorts: Randomized trial of newly onboarding accounts + a stratified sample of mid-volume enterprise customers (tiered by monthly spend: <$1k, $1k-$10k, >$10k).
- Variants: Control (current per-token symmetric pricing, no streaming microfloor) vs. Treatment A (output-weighted discount only) vs. Treatment B (streaming microfloor only) vs. Treatment C (both changes).
- Pricing matrix (example):
  * Input token price = $0.0006/token (baseline)
  * Output token price (treatment) = $0.00054/token (10% discount)
  * Streaming microfloor = $0.50/session if streamed output > 150 tokens within session; otherwise no floor.
- Duration: 6 weeks active + 2 weeks pre-rollout stabilization + 1 week measurement window.
- Sample size/Power: target N ~ 2,500 accounts split across cohorts to detect a 4% difference in ARPU with 90% power (finance/analytics to verify).

Instrumentation and telemetry:
- Required metrics: ARPU (per-account, per-session), tokens_in, tokens_out, stream_sessions, sessions_below_floor, average session length, churn at 30/60 days, cost-per-token (marginal GPU), model-selection frequency, latency P50/P95, billing disputes count.
- Events/flags: mark sessions as STREAMED=true; record session-level token totals and applied floor credits. Add new billing dimension token_direction (input|output).
- Dashboards: temporary experiment dashboard in Console -> Pricing Experiments with cohort breakdown, daily revenue delta, and cost delta.

Success criteria (primary):
- Treatment C increases per-account revenue by >=3% and does not increase churn (30d churn delta <= +0.5pp).
- Unit economics: marginal cost increase <= 2% (finance).
- No material rise in billing disputes or operational incidents linked to metering changes.

Success criteria (secondary):
- Increased usage of higher-output models by >2pp in treatment vs control.
- Favorable customer sentiment in NPS/qualitative feedback for enterprise cohort.

Risks and mitigations:
- Metering/edge cases: mis-tagged streaming sessions could cause over/under-billing. Mitigation: add strict unit tests, shadow-run billing calculation for 2 weeks before charging.
- Customer confusion: new microfloor semantics may be non-intuitive. Mitigation: in-console hover text, a one-time email to impacted users, and opt-in for pilot enterprise customers.
- Gaming: customers might artificially inflate outputs to get discounts. Mitigation: detect anomalous output/inbound patterns and cap discounts for suspicious behavior; include this as a monitoring alert.

Dependencies:
- Billing pipeline changes (ENG-BILL-2025): apply token_direction dimension and microfloor logic in billing engine.
- Console UI flag & price exposure (ENG-CONSOLE-3741).
- Analytics cohort instrumentation (ENG-ANALYTICS-1982).
- Legal & Contracts review for enterprise T&C updates (Legal ticket: LEG-1129).

Rollout plan:
1) Shadow run: implement pricing logic in billing but do not apply charges; run shadow for 14 days (verify metrics and reconcile).
2) Small opt-in enterprise pilot (10 accounts) for 2 weeks with direct CS/solutions monitoring.
3) Ramp to randomized trial across self-serve + stratified enterprise cohorts for full experiment duration.
4) If success criteria met, phased default rollout with clear console disclosure and updated docs; otherwise revert all changes and document learnings.

Customer communication:
- Pilot customers will receive a one-pager + scheduled sync to collect feedback.
- For any general rollout we will add console banners, FAQ, and a billing calculator showing sample sessions.

Artifacts and links:
- Experiment spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pricing/per-token-elasticity-2025
- Billing design doc (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/billing-per-token-elasticity
- Analytics dashboard (internal): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/pricing-experiments-47812
- Related Linear tickets: PM-41207, ENG-3741, ENG-ANALYTICS-1982

Approvals required:
- Finance: revenue impact sign-off (K. Huang)
- Legal: contract and enterprise T&C changes (Legal: LEG-1129)
- Security/Compliance: billing telemetry review (security_review_required=true)

Notes:
- We intentionally pick a conservative output discount (10%) to test customer elasticity without endangering unit economics.
- If outputs grow materially (>10% output share delta), we will run additional experiments to calibrate multi-tier discounts by customer segment.
